# Component

`DualStorageRouter.reconcileCategoryWithPathGuard()` in `src/storage/dualStorageRouter.ts`
(the per-category counterpart of the `md_root:<category>` path-guard used by `reconcile()`).

# The bug (commit `08fbdda2`, ticket 06, neuron-2.3.0)

On a category's **first-ever sighting** (i.e. when `vectorDb.getMeta(metaKey)` returned
`null` because there was no recorded `md_root:<category>` value yet — either a brand-new
category, or, after this ticket's change, a category whose `categories.<name>.storage`
override newly started resolving to `md` for the first time), the old code only recorded
the current resolved root:

```ts
if (knownRoot === null) {
  this.vectorDb.setMeta(metaKey, resolvedRoot);
} else if (knownRoot !== resolvedRoot) {
  await this.seedCategoryFromVector(category);
  ...
}
```

It then **fell through to the normal, destructive strict-mirror `reconcileCategory` path**
instead of returning. That mirror trusts the on-disk `.md` file as authoritative and deletes
any vector rows not found in it. Since the category had never been written to markdown
before, its `.md` file was empty (or non-existent), so every existing vector row for that
category was treated as "absent from markdown" and deleted — silent, real data loss.

This was previously masked because, before ticket 06 made `categories.<name>.storage`
"always live," a category could only enter the md-reconciled set in a stable way (its
storage mode didn't change shape between runs), so a first sighting always coincided with a
genuinely empty category. Making the per-category override always-live broke that
assumption: an existing category with real vector rows (e.g. one previously pinned to
`vector` storage, or under a `storage.mode: md` config where `categories.foo.storage: vector`
used to be silently ignored) could suddenly resolve to `md` for the first time while already
holding vector data — triggering the destructive fallthrough on real data.

# The fix

The first-ever-sighting branch (`knownRoot === null`) is now treated exactly like a
*changed*-root branch: instead of just recording the root and falling through to the
destructive mirror, it re-exports/reseeds that category's markdown from the vector index
(the same authoritative source `bootstrapSeed` uses, via `seedCategoryFromVector`), records
the new root, and returns immediately — skipping the destructive mirror entirely for that
call:

```ts
if (knownRoot === null || knownRoot !== resolvedRoot) {
  await this.seedCategoryFromVector(category);
  this.vectorDb.setMeta(metaKey, resolvedRoot);
  return;
}
```

For a genuinely brand-new category with no vector rows yet, this reseed is just a harmless
zero-row export; for a category with existing vector data being reconciled for the first
time, it now safely reconstructs the markdown file from the vector store instead of wiping
the vector rows because the markdown file was empty.

results.finishSummary: DualStorageRouter's reconcileCategoryWithPathGuard used to fall through to the destructive strict-mirror mode on a category's first-ever sighting (deleting vector rows not present in the never-before-written .md file); it now reseeds the category from the vector index the same way it already did for changed roots, avoiding data loss when the always-live per-category storage override newly surfaces existing categories.

# Component and Bug

**Component:** `DualStorageRouter.reconcileCategoryWithPathGuard` (in `src/storage/dualStorageRouter.ts`), specifically its handling of `md_root:<category>` metadata during `reconcile`.

## Old (buggy) behavior
On a category's **first-ever sighting** (i.e. `knownRoot === null` — either an upgrade from a pre-ticket-05 store or a brand-new category with no recorded root), the code just recorded the current resolved root via `vectorDb.setMeta(metaKey, resolvedRoot)` and then **fell through** into the normal `reconcileCategory` path, which runs a destructive "strict mirror": it treats the (empty/never-before-written) `.md` file as authoritative and deletes any vector rows for that category not found in the markdown file.

This was safe under ticket 05's assumptions (every category reaching this code had already been reconciled once, so a first sighting only really happened for genuinely empty categories). Ticket 06 broke that assumption by making the per-category `categories.<name>.storage` override **always live** instead of only active in `split` mode — so a category could now newly enter `mdCategories()` for the first time even though it already had real rows in the vector store (e.g. flipping a category's override from `vector` to `md`, or removing a `categories.foo.storage: vector` override that used to be silently ignored). In that case, the strict-mirror fallthrough would read the never-written `.md` file as empty and delete every vector row for that category — silent, real data loss.

## New (fixed) behavior
Both the first-ever-sighting case (`knownRoot === null`) and the changed-root case (`knownRoot !== resolvedRoot`) are now handled identically: instead of falling through to the destructive mirror, the router **reseeds** the category by re-exporting it from the vector index (the authoritative source, same one `bootstrapSeed` uses) into its resolved markdown location, records the new root, and returns — deferring the strict mirror to the *next* reconcile call. For a genuinely brand-new category with no data in either store, this reseed is just a harmless zero-row export, so the fix costs nothing in the case the old code was designed for while eliminating the new data-loss window opened by the always-live per-category override.

results.finishSummary: DualStorageRouter.reconcileCategoryWithPathGuard's first-sighting branch used to fall through to the destructive strict-mirror reconcile (deleting vector rows it saw as "absent" from an empty/never-written .md file); it now reseeds the category from the vector index (same as a changed-root sighting) before returning, avoiding data loss.

(the per-category path-guard branch of `reconcile()`, fixed in commit `08fbdda2`,
ticket 06 / neuron-2.3.0).

# Old (buggy) behavior

`reconcileCategoryWithPathGuard` tracks, per category, the last resolved md-root it
reconciled against via a `md_root:<category>` metadata key. On a **first-ever sighting**
of a category (i.e. `knownRoot === null` — an upgrade from a pre-ticket-05 store, or a

reconcile call for that category proceeds normally (mirror-based). For a genuinely

# Component with the bug

`DualStorageRouter.reconcileCategoryWithPathGuard` (in `src/storage/dualStorageRouter.ts`), specifically its per-category md-root path-guard logic used by the storage-reconcile path (`reconcile()` → `reconcileCategoryWithPathGuard()` → `reconcileCategory()`).

This surfaced while making ticket 06's config change: `categories.<name>.storage` was changed from being inert unless `storage.mode: split` was set, to being an "always-live" override that takes effect under every top-level storage mode (`resolveCategoryStorage()`: `categories.<name>.storage > storage.mode > 'md'`).

# Old (buggy) behavior

On a category's *first-ever sighting* (i.e. `knownRoot === null`, meaning the router had never recorded a resolved md-root/metadata key for that category before), the code only recorded the current resolved root via `vectorDb.setMeta(metaKey, resolvedRoot)` and then **fell through** into the normal `reconcileCategory` destructive "strict mirror" reconcile — the logic that treats the on-disk `.md` file as authoritative and deletes any vector rows not found in it.

This was safe under the old (pre-ticket-06) rules because a category could only ever reach this code path after having already been reconciled at least once before — the set of categories being reconciled never changed shape between runs. But once the per-category `storage` override became always-live, a category with existing, real vector-only data could newly enter `mdCategories()` (the reconciled set) for the first time — e.g. a `storage.mode: md` config with `categories.foo.storage: vector` removed/changed to `md`. In that case the "first sighting" fallthrough would read the category's never-before-written (and thus empty) `.md` file as the source of truth and delete every one of that category's existing vector rows as "absent from markdown" — silent, real data loss.

# New (fixed) behavior

Both a first-ever sighting (`knownRoot === null`) and a changed root (`knownRoot !== resolvedRoot`) now take the same branch: instead of falling through to the destructive strict mirror, the router **reseeds** — it re-exports that category's existing data from the vector index (treated as authoritative) into its resolved markdown location via `seedCategoryFromVector(category)`, then records the new root via `vectorDb.setMeta(metaKey, resolvedRoot)` and returns, deferring the normal mirror reconcile to the *next* call. For a genuinely brand-new category with nothing in either store, this reseed is just a harmless zero-row export.

results.finishSummary: The bug was in DualStorageRouter.reconcileCategoryWithPathGuard: on a category's first-ever sighting it used to fall through to the destructive markdown-mirror and delete all pre-existing vector rows (since the never-written .md file read as empty); now it seeds markdown from the vector store first (like a root change) before any mirror runs, preventing that data loss.

# Component

`DualStorageRouter.reconcileCategoryWithPathGuard` (and the first-ever-sighting
branch it guards) in `src/storage/dualStorageRouter.ts`, part of the
markdown/vector storage-reconcile path.

# Trigger

Ticket 06 (neuron-2.3.0) made the per-category `categories.<name>.storage`
config override *always live* (previously it was only honored under the
now-deleted `split` top-level storage mode, and was otherwise ignored). This
meant a category could now enter `mdCategories()` for the very first time on
a store that already had real, populated vector rows for it — e.g. a config
that used to run `storage.mode: md` with `categories.foo.storage: vector`
(silently ignored before) now actually resolving `foo` to vector, or a
category whose override flips from `vector` to `md`.

# Old (buggy) behavior

On a category's first-ever sighting in `reconcileCategoryWithPathGuard`, the
code just recorded the category's resolved root and fell straight through
into the normal destructive mirror (`reconcileCategory`). That mirror reads
the category's markdown file — which, for a category seeing this path for
the first time, had never been written — as empty, and then deletes every
vector row for that category because none of them are "present in markdown."
This logic was only safe under the old assumption (true in ticket 05's world)
that every category reaching this method had already been reconciled at
least once before, so "no prior root on record" only ever meant a changed
root, never a truly first sighting with pre-existing vector data. Ticket 06
broke that assumption, turning the fallthrough into real, silent data loss:
an existing vector-backed category's data was wiped the moment its resolved
storage flipped to `md` for the first time.

# New (fixed) behavior

`reconcileCategoryWithPathGuard` now treats a first-ever sighting the same
way it already treated a genuine root change: instead of falling through to
the destructive mirror, it calls `seedCategoryFromVector(category)` to
re-export the category's existing vector rows into markdown at its resolved
location, records the resolved root in `md_root:<category>` meta, and
returns — leaving the destructive mirror (`reconcileCategory`) to run only on
the *next* reconcile call, once markdown genuinely reflects the vector store.
For a brand-new category with nothing in either store, this seed is just a
harmless zero-row export, so the fix costs nothing in the common case while
closing the data-loss window for categories with pre-existing vector data.

# Recall hook character budget

**Granularity: per epoch, not per session.**

The budget (`recall.epochCharBudget` in `neuron.yaml`, implemented in
`src/config/neuronYaml.ts` and consumed in `src/commands/hook.ts` /
`src/harnesses/ledger.ts`) is tracked per **epoch**, where an epoch is the
span between session start (or the last compaction) and the next
`context-reset` event — *not* the whole session. Because `context-reset`
wipes everything neuron previously injected (ADR 0014 §5), re-injecting
after a reset is recovery rather than repetition, so the budget resets
with the ledger (`rollEpoch`) rather than accumulating across an entire
session. A single session can therefore span multiple epochs, each with
its own fresh budget.

## Default value

- Default: **18,000 characters** (`epochCharBudget: 18000`).
- Composition: 6,000 chars reserved for the session-start architecture
  card (`SESSION_START_CHAR_BUDGET`) plus up to 8 worst-case full
  `pre-prompt` turns at `PRE_PROMPT_CHAR_BUDGET` (1,500 chars each).

## Published unit

The budget is published/described externally as **~6,000 tokens**, using
a conservative **3 characters per token** ratio (as already used in
`src/harnesses/payload.ts`), rather than the more common 4:1 chars/token
ratio — chosen deliberately to overstate neuron's own cost rather than
understate it.

## Behavior once exhausted

Once the epoch's budget is exhausted (`remainingEpochBudget(...) <= 0`),
the hook performs a **hard stop** for the rest of that epoch:
- On `pre-prompt`, it skips the query entirely (no injection) but still
  records the turn (with zero content) so the per-turn cost-rate
  denominator stays accurate.
- It does **not** degrade to showing everything or repeating unseen
  content — it goes silent for that epoch. The only way to get injections
  again is a new epoch (triggered by `context-reset`, which rolls/resets
  the ledger and budget), or by not having a session id at all, in which
  case there's no epoch to track and the hook falls back to the simpler
  fixed per-injection cap (`SESSION_START_CHAR_BUDGET` /
  `PRE_PROMPT_CHAR_BUDGET`) without a running total.

# Recall hook char budget

**Tracked per-epoch, not per-session.** `epochCharBudget` (in `src/config/neuronYaml.ts`, `neuron.yaml`'s `recall` config, default below) is enforced by `remainingEpochBudget` in `src/harnesses/ledger.ts`, keyed by `sessionId` but scoped to the current **epoch** — the span from session start (or the last compaction) to the next `context-reset`. A single session can contain multiple epochs: `rollEpoch` resets both the dedupe ledger and the char-spend counter together whenever a compaction/`context-reset` happens, because compaction wipes out everything neuron previously injected, so re-injection after it is "recovery, not repetition," not a continuation of the same budget window.

- **Default numeric budget:** 18,000 characters (`epochCharBudget: z.number().int().positive().default(18000)` in `src/config/neuronYaml.ts`).
- **Published unit / conversion:** the cost summary (`summarizeRecallCost` in `src/harnesses/ledger.ts`, surfaced via `neuron status`) also reports an approximate token figure using a fixed ratio of **3 characters per token** (`CHARS_PER_TOKEN_RATIO = 3`), i.e. `epochTokenBudgetApprox = ceil(epochCharBudget / 3)` — 18,000 chars ≈ 6,000 tokens by default.
- **What happens once exhausted:** once `remainingEpochBudget(...) <= 0` for the current epoch, the `pre-prompt` hook hits a hard stop (ticket 07): it records the turn (with zero chars/ids, so the per-turn cost-rate denominator still counts silent turns) but skips querying memory entirely — no further recall content is injected for the rest of that epoch. Injection resumes only once a new epoch starts (i.e. after `rollEpoch` fires on `context-reset`/compaction), at which point the budget resets to `epochCharBudget` again. (If there's no `sessionId` at all, there's no ledger/budget to track against, so the hook deliberately degrades toward showing everything every turn rather than toward silence.)

# Recall hook character budget

**Tracked per epoch, not per session.** An "epoch" is the span from session start (or
the last compaction) to the next `context-reset`, not the whole session — because
compaction wipes everything neuron previously injected, so re-injection after a
compaction is recovery, not repetition. `rollEpoch` resets both the dedupe ledger and
the char-spend counter together when a `context-reset` fires, so a single session can
contain multiple epochs, each getting its own fresh budget (`src/harnesses/ledger.ts`).

- **Default numeric budget:** `epochCharBudget` defaults to **18,000 characters**
  (`src/config/neuronYaml.ts`, `z.number().int().positive().default(18000)`).
- **Published unit:** the budget is reported to users in *tokens*, not raw characters.
  `summarizeRecallCost` converts it via a fixed ratio `CHARS_PER_TOKEN_RATIO = 3`
  (i.e. 3 chars/token), publishing `epochTokenBudgetApprox = ceil(epochCharBudget / 3)`
  — so the default 18,000-char budget is published as ~6,000 tokens
  (`src/harnesses/ledger.ts`).
- **What happens once exhausted:** the hook enforces a hard stop, not gradual
  degradation. Once `remainingEpochBudget(...) <= 0` for the current epoch, the
  `pre-prompt` hook records the turn (with zero chars/ids, so the per-turn cost rate
  still has silent turns in its denominator) and skips the memory query entirely —
  nothing further is injected until the epoch rolls over via the next `context-reset`
  (`src/commands/hook.ts`). Within an epoch, the session-start architecture-card
  injection and each pre-prompt turn's injection are additionally capped by their own
  fixed per-injection limits (`SESSION_START_CHAR_BUDGET = 6000`,
  `PRE_PROMPT_CHAR_BUDGET = 1500`, in `src/harnesses/payload.ts`), and whichever of the
  epoch's remaining budget or these per-injection caps is smaller wins.
